name: Client Hint: device model
plain: Android phone or tablet model name, only when the site asks.
meaning: Exposes the exact handset (Pixel 8, SM-S928B). Informs device-specific bugs and ad targeting. iOS never exposes a model; desktop returns an empty string.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: model
fields.range: Hundreds of Android model codes; empty on desktop

limits.headline: Can see the model name of your Android phone or tablet when it asks
limits.user_action: Nothing. The site asks and Chrome on Android answers without a prompt
can: Learn the exact model, such as Pixel 8 or a Samsung code
Fix bugs or tune the page for that handset
Use the model for ad targeting
Spot the same phone again as one clue among several
cannot: See an iPhone or iPad model; Apple never shares it
Get a model name from a desktop; it comes back empty
Get an answer until the site asks for it
limits.differs: Android Chrome shares it. iPhone never does, and desktops return an empty answer.

story.what_it_is: Tells a site the exact model of your Android phone or tablet when it asks.

marketing.name: User-Agent Client Hints
marketing.pitch: Chrome's way of letting sites ask for specifics like model only when they need them.

story.for_you: You never see it. If it works well, a site might avoid a bug that only hits your phone model. If it works badly, it can feed a stored profile about the phone you own.
story.for_makers: Developers use the model to fix bugs that only happen on certain phones. Advertisers can aim at owners of premium handsets. Fraud tools look for fake models used by emulators and farms of cheap devices.

use_cases.example: A bug report from a web app shows it only breaks on one Galaxy model, so the team ships a targeted fix.
An accessory seller shows a case for the exact phone model the visitor uses.
A browser game turns off particles for a known low-power phone model but keeps them on a flagship.
A streaming service chooses an HDR stream only for models that handle it properly.
A fraud system flags a visit from an emulator model name used by bot farms.
A web chat support widget prefills your phone model in a help request.

technical_bounds: Empty string on desktop and iOS

history.change: Android UA shows model as K; hint is the only source
